class.name: WindServer
class.brief_description: The world's wind, shared by foliage shaders, physics bodies, cloth and scripts.
class.description: The one global wind of the world. Everything that reacts to wind reads it here, so grass, trees, cloth and bodies all move with the same gusts. The wind at a point is the mean wind ([member speed] toward [member direction_degrees]) plus gusts: a noise pattern [member gust_scale] meters across that travels with the wind, so gust fronts sweep across grass fields at the wind's speed. Gusts also swing the direction by up to [member direction_swing_degrees]. [b]Shaders:[/b] the server sets the global shader parameters [code]wind_mean[/code], [code]wind_gust[/code] and [code]wind_motion[/code] (all [code]vec4[/code]) every frame. Include the built-in shader include at [method get_shader_include_path] to use [code]wind_sample()[/code], [code]wind_grass_offset()[/code] and [code]wind_tree_offset()[/code]; the comment at the top of the include shows how. The noise is the same as in [method sample], so a shader and a script see the same wind at the same point. [GrassField3D]'s default material uses it. [b]Physics:[/b] add a [WindReceiver3D] to a [RigidBody3D]. [PhysXCloth3D] adds this wind when [member PhysXCloth3D.use_global_wind] is on. The startup values come from the [code]weather/wind/*[/code] project settings. The wind moves in the editor too. [codeblock] WindServer.speed = 12.0 WindServer.direction_degrees = 90.0 # Toward +X. var wind := WindServer.sample(global_position) # m/s at this point, gusts included. [/codeblock]

method.name: advance
method.description: Moves the gust pattern on by [param delta] seconds (times [member time_scale]). Called every frame while [member auto_update] is on.

method.name: get_direction
method.description: The direction the mean wind blows toward, horizontal and of unit length.

method.name: get_gust_factor
method.description: The wind's speed at [param position] relative to the mean [member speed]: above [code]1.0[/code] in a gust, below in a lull.

method.name: get_mean_wind
method.description: The mean wind velocity in meters per second, without gusts.

method.name: get_shader_include_code
method.description: The source of the wind shader include, for example to copy it into a project file and change it.

method.name: get_shader_include_path
method.description: The path of the built-in wind shader include, [code]"res://.builtin/wind.gdshaderinc"[/code]. It is served from memory, so [code]#include[/code] finds it in every project and in exported games without a file.

method.name: sample
method.description: The wind velocity at a world [param position], in meters per second, gusts included. The wind is horizontal ([code]y[/code] is [code]0[/code]). Thread-safe.

members.member: Air density in kg/m³, used by [WindReceiver3D] for the drag force. [code]1.225[/code] is air at sea level.
If [code]true[/code], the gust pattern moves on every frame by itself. Turn it off to drive it with [method advance], for example in deterministic tests.
Heading of the wind in degrees: [code]0[/code] blows toward -Z, increasing clockwise seen from above ([code]90[/code] blows toward +X).
How far gusts swing the wind's direction at [member gustiness] [code]1.0[/code], in degrees.
Size of the gusts in meters.
How much the wind varies in gusts, from [code]0.0[/code] (steady) to [code]1.0[/code]. At [code]1.0[/code] the speed ranges from about 0.6 to 2 times [member speed].
Mean wind speed in meters per second.
Speed of the gust pattern's motion. [code]0.0[/code] freezes the gusts in place; the mean wind still blows.
Small-scale unsteadiness, from [code]0.0[/code] to [code]1.0[/code]: how much grass blades and leaves flutter.
